research.caveats:
1. How the prices were collected: only the WebSearch tool was used (extended mode, October 2026). WebFetch does not work here, so no page was opened. Every price comes from search-result snippets and summaries of the listed URLs. Most pages carry no date, the search tool flagged a few as old (for example Apollo ferritin, about 446 days), and some show conflicting figures on the same page. Prices should be spot-checked on the live pages before final pricing.

2. Two price groups: for most mid-priced tests (Vitamin D, B12, ferritin, LFT, lipid), online platforms (Tata 1mg, Healthians, Redcliffe, PharmEasy) show deep-discount promo prices of 30-70% off a high MRP. Established brands (Dr Lal PathLabs, Metropolis, Thyrocare, Apollo, Max, Agilus) show list prices 2-4 times higher. The 'typical' figure is roughly the median across both groups. For a NABL walk-in lab, the established-brand band is the closer comparison and the promo band is the price floor customers see online. Example: Vitamin D runs about Rs 300-650 on promo versus Rs 1,230-1,840 at established labs.

3. Dr Lal PathLabs Nagpur: the prices (CBC 250, FBS 70, HbA1c 430, lipid basic 770, LFT 790, KFT 840, TSH 220, Vitamin D 1,230, ferritin 650) come from search summaries of lalpathlabs.com Nagpur pages, mainly the city page lalpathlabs.com/test/city/nagpur, and diagnosticcentres.in shows near-identical figures. B12 (Rs 1,180) has its own Nagpur URL.

4. No Nagpur-specific page was found for these, so chain prices from other cities or national pages are used, with the city recorded on each source:
- Reticulocyte count: chains other than local Medifee listings
- Cystatin C: Dr Lal, Redcliffe, Metropolis, Thyrocare, Healthians, PharmEasy, Apollo
- CPK: Dr Lal, Redcliffe, Thyrocare, Tata 1mg

5. Medifee data: local Nagpur labs and hospitals (Wockhardt Heart Hospital, Rainbow Medinova, Medcis, Kiran, Rajat, Nagpur Reference Pathology) come only from Medifee listings. These are often several years old. The 'low' values for CBC (130), reticulocyte (150), lipid (195), KFT (350), TSH (120) and CPK (100) rest on them.

6. Hospitals not found: no published lab prices turned up for Orange City, Alexis, Kingsway, CARE or Wockhardt hospitals, apart from Wockhardt via Medifee.

7. Panel definitions differ: lipid (mini, basic or advance), KFT (with or without electrolytes), and TSH (ultrasensitive or 3rd generation).

8. Home-collection fees: a small order (for example fasting glucose alone) can attract a charge; one Thyrocare reseller lists Rs 200 for orders under Rs 500.

9. Excluded: Active B12, Vitamin D 1,25-dihydroxy and CK-MB are different tests and were left out. The DocMitra fasting glucose price of Rs 480 is listed as a source but treated as an outlier and kept out of the high value.

verify.issues:
I ran no fresh searches. My first WebSearch calls were refused because the run had used its limit of 200 WebSearch calls per turn, shared across all agents. I did not work around the limit, so no new sources were added. Every verdict re-analyses the researcher's own cited data: I recomputed medians, checked that each test matched, removed outliers, and checked consistency across sources. Read 'confirmed' as 'consistent with the cited evidence', not 'independently re-verified'. To finish independent verification, send a follow-up message, or raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION.

Problems that affect several tests:
(1) MaxAtHome is Max Healthcare's premium home-care service, and it charges 1.2 to 2.3 times what the same group's Max Lab charges for the same test (CBC Rs 424 vs 250, ferritin Rs 1,520 vs 650, lipid Rs 1,067 vs 600, CPK Rs 600 vs 300). I excluded it from the high values.
(2) The lows for CBC (Rs 130), reticulocyte (Rs 150), lipid (Rs 195), TSH (Rs 120) and CPK (Rs 100) rest only on undated Medifee local listings. I raised them to the lowest current listed price; Medifee is kept only as a possible local floor. The Medifee 'average' cited for ferritin points to a single lab's page.
(3) Wrong test matched: the Metropolis reticulocyte source (Rs 450) is the immature reticulocyte fraction page. Possible wrong match: the Redcliffe TSH source is a general thyroid-test page and may be the thyroid profile.
(4) PharmEasy sources for B12 and CPK are labelled Nagpur, but their URLs are national pages.
(5) Vitamin D, B12, ferritin, LFT and Cystatin C have bimodal prices: online promo prices versus established-lab list prices. A single 'typical' median lands in different places for each: at the bottom of the established band for Vitamin D (Rs 1,250), but in the gap between the bands for B12 (Rs 800). For a NABL walk-in benchmark, the established-lab bands are Vitamin D Rs 1,230-1,500, B12 Rs 1,090-1,260, ferritin Rs 650-900 and Cystatin C Rs 1,100-1,300.
(6) Dr Lal's Nagpur figures mostly come from a search summary of the city page, not from individual test pages.
(7) No chain gives a Nagpur price for reticulocyte, and only two Nagpur prices exist for Cystatin C.

All prices still need a spot-check on the live pages before final pricing.

I found 36 packages from 12 providers, and 18 of them are Nagpur-specific listings. The providers are Redcliffe, Healthians, Tata 1mg, Dr Lal, Apollo Diagnostics/Apollo Clinic, Thyrocare, Metropolis, MyDiagnostics, Wockhardt, KIMS-Kingsway, CARE, Arneja and Alexis/Max. - Wockhardt Basic: 1,799 to 1,499 to 1,200.

2) PACKAGE PRICE VS ACTUAL SUM OF INDIVIDUAL TESTS. I priced the individual tests at Dr Lal Nagpur (lalpathlabs.com/test/city/nagpur), whose list prices are typical of NABL walk-in labs:
